Statement: I can identify how an author uses a character's actions and feelings to reveal a big idea or theme.
I can use a sticky note to record a detail and the big idea it represents.
I can identify challenges a character faces in a story.
I can explain how a character responds to a challenge and how that response connects to a story's theme.
I can identify how characters interact with each other in a story.
I can explain how these interactions develop the story's themes.
I can identify important settings in a story.
I can explain how a setting influences a character's feelings or actions.
I can connect the influence of setting to a story's theme.
I can combine my understanding of characters, their interactions, and settings to identify a major theme.
I can explain how different story elements work together to develop a theme.
I can identify specific words an author uses to describe a character.
I can explain how these words help me understand the character better and hint at a theme.
I can identify similes and metaphors in a story.
I can explain what a simile or metaphor means in the context of the story.
I can connect figurative language to the development of character and theme.
I can identify hyperbole and personification in a story.
I can explain how these literary devices add to the story's meaning.
I can connect these devices to character development and theme.
I can identify an author's specific craft choices (word choice, figurative language).
I can explain how these craft choices strengthen a story's theme.
I can identify who is telling the story (the narrator).
I can explain how different narrators have different feelings and thoughts about events.
I can explain how a narrator's point of view shapes what I learn about other characters.
I can recognize that characters might be seen differently depending on who is telling the story.
I can identify chapters told from different characters' points of view.
I can explain how switching narrators helps me get a fuller picture of the story and its themes.
I can explain how point of view influences the author's craft choices (word choice, figurative language).
I can show how both point of view and craft work together to develop a story's themes.
I can identify the main characters and setting in a new story ('The One and Only Ivan').
I can make initial predictions about potential themes based on early character and setting details.
I can identify emerging themes in 'The One and Only Ivan' based on character actions and events.
I can support my identified themes with textual evidence from the book.
I can identify a challenge faced by a character in 'Wonder' and 'The One and Only Ivan.'
I can compare and contrast how characters from both books respond to similar challenges.
I can explain how their responses reveal different facets of a shared theme.
I can identify a common theme present in both 'Wonder' and 'The One and Only Ivan.'
I can use evidence from both texts to support the identified common theme.
I can identify a shared theme across 'Wonder' and 'The One and Only Ivan.'
I can explain how each author uses different literary devices (e.g., word choice, figurative language, point of view) to develop that same theme.
I can select a common theme from 'Wonder' and 'The One and Only Ivan.'
I can gather strong textual evidence from both books... to support the chosen theme.
I can organize my evidence using a graphic organizer in preparation for a final project.
I can use my graphic organizer to plan a presentation or poster that compares how two authors develop a shared theme.
I can organize my ideas logically for a clear presentation.
I can create a poster or deliver a presentation that effectively compares how two authors develop a shared theme.
I can use textual evidence and explain author's craft to support my claims.
I can present my ideas clearly and confidently (for presentations).
